transcript.text: Thank you, Maya. Here's my status update. I had a call with HelioGrid's commercial sponsor to go over the business terms, and what I learned creates some significant gaps between what HelioGrid proposed and what they'll actually agree to. The key discrepancies are: First, the proposed draft describes a worldwide exclusive license, but the approved business term sheet permits exclusivity only for grid-scale battery storage applications — not a broad, unrestricted exclusive license. Second, the proposed draft sets the royalty at 5% of net sales, but the approved term sheet specifies a royalty of exactly 6% of net sales. Third, the proposed draft allows unrestricted sublicensing, but the approved term sheet prohibits sublicensing entirely. I should also note that HelioGrid's commercial sponsor indicated they will not sign on the broader draft terms as currently written. I have not yet entered the call terms into the deal tracker, which I'll need to do promptly. So to summarize, we have three material deviations from the approved business terms — scope of exclusivity, royalty rate, and sublicensing rights — and HelioGrid has signaled they won't accept the broader terms as drafted. I'd like to get these reconciled before we move forward.
